battle.name: 隋煬帝第一次攻高麗之戰
battle.brief: 大業八年正月，隋煬帝自涿郡御師東征，二十四道大軍一百一十三萬餘人，旌旗亙九百六十里。三月渡遼水、圍遼東城，五月後會兵鴨綠水西；追乙支文德至薩水遭四面鈔擊，全軍潰散，一日一夜奔回四百五十里。卡面亞述長矛早於本役一千五百餘年，僅作槊矛形制之源；隋軍近身所恃為槊、排甲與百日糧。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 大業八年（612）正月，隋朝以一紙詔書把全國的兵調到了幽州涿郡，兵分左右各十二軍，限期會師平壤；對面的高句麗則以國都平壤與鴨綠水天險為核心，調集的是熟悉山地的少量精兵。隋方的指揮系統高度集中：一切由天子御前決定，四方兵集涿郡之後，隋煬帝親授節度，規定每軍設大將、亞將各一人，騎兵四十隊（每隊百人，十隊為團），步卒八十隊分為四團、每團設偏將一人，鎧冑、纓拂、旗幡按團各異色，輜重散兵也編為四團由步卒挾帶行軍，進止立營皆有定制，並另設不受大將節制的受降使者；御營則合十一衛、三台、五省、九寺，分隸內外前後左右六軍。出兵的道次是編定死的：左十二軍出鏤方，經長岑、溟海、蓋馬、建安、南蘇、遼東、玄菟、扶餘、朝鮮、沃沮、樂浪等道；右十二軍出黏蟬、含資、渾彌、臨屯、候城、提奚、蹋頓、肅慎、碣石、帶方、襄平等道。分道主將分別是宇文述出扶餘道、于仲文出樂浪道、荊元恆出遼東道、薛世雄出沃沮道、辛世雄出玄菟道、張瑾出襄平道、趙孝才出碣石道、崔弘昇出遂城道、衛文昇出增地道、段文振出南蘇道，另有左屯衛大將軍麥鐵杖自請為先鋒，以及率江淮水軍的右翊衛大將軍來護兒。高句麗方面，國王高元坐鎮平壤，統兵大將乙支文德負責鴨綠水一線的遲滯與反擊，國都之外的邊城則由各城主與部將分守。第三方是百濟：百濟王璋主動請隋軍討伐高句麗、派臣國智牟來請師期，隋廷大喜並派起部郎席律告知會期，但璋同時又與高句麗暗中相通，隋軍渡遼之後百濟只在國境上整兵，聲稱響應，實際上持兩端。
countriesEn: In the first month of 612, the eighth year of the Daye era, the Sui dynasty moved the armed men of the whole empire to Zhuo Commandery in You prefecture, splitting them into a left and a right group of twelve armies each with a fixed rendezvous at Pyongyang; opposite them, the kingdom of Goguryeo based itself on the capital of Pyongyang and the natural barrier of the Yalu river, and committed to it a small force of troops experienced in the northern mountains. The Sui command system was highly centralised: everything was decided in the emperor's presence, and once the troops of the realm had gathered at Zhuo, Emperor Yang himself issued the deployment orders, directing that each army have one commander and one deputy, that cavalry be organised in forty units of a hundred men each with ten units to a regiment, that infantry be organised in eighty units divided into four regiments with an officer over each, that armour, plumes and banners be coloured differently for every regiment, that baggage troops and stragglers form four more regiments to be carried along by the infantry, and that camps, marches and halts all follow a fixed ceremonial order, with a separate commissioner for receiving surrender who was not subject to the authority of the army commanders; the imperial camp itself combined the eleven guards, the three platforms, the five ministries and the nine temples, distributed among the inner, outer, front, rear, left and right armies. The lines of march were fixed in advance: the left twelve armies set out from Loulang by way of Changceng, Minghai, Gema, Jian'an, Nansu, Liaodong, Xuantu, Fuyu, Chaoxian, Wozhu and Lelang; the right twelve set out from Nianchan by way of Hanzhi, Hunmi, Lintun, Houcheng, Tixi, Tadun, Sushen, Jieshi, Daifang, Xiangping and other circuits. The named commanders were Yuwen Shu on the Fuyu road, Yu Zhongwen on the Lelang road, Jing Yuanheng on the Liaodong road, Xue Shixiong on the Wozhu road, Xin Shixiong on the Xuantu road, Zhang Jin on the Xiangping road, Zhao Xiaocai on the Jieshi road, Cui Hongsheng on the Suicheng road, Wei Wensheng on the Zengdi road and Duan Wenzhen on the Nansu road; there were also Mai Tiezhang of the Left Imperial Guard, who volunteered as vanguard, and Lai Hu'er, who led the river fleet from the Jiang and Huai. On the Goguryeo side the king, Gao Yuan, remained at Pyongyang, and the field command on the Yalu line was held by the general Yizhi Wende, while the border cities were held by their own local commanders and captains. The third party was Baekje: its king, Zhang, offered to join the war against Goguryeo and sent his minister Guozhi Mou to learn the date of the operation, which the Sui court received with generous rewards, sending the director of the Ministry of Works, Xi Lü, to announce the appointed time; but Zhang was at the same time in secret communication with Goguryeo, and when the Sui army crossed the Liao river Baekje merely mustered troops along its own frontier, professing assistance while in fact keeping to both sides.
people: 這一役是隋煬帝的意志與眾多將領的失誤共同造成的。煬帝在正月壬午下詔，癸未第一軍出發，御營隨軍東行，在南桑干水社天、於臨朔宮南類上帝、於薊城北祭馬祖，儀式做完才拔營；出發前他還問征合水令庚質，高句麗之眾不能當他一郡，這一仗是否可取，庚質答伐之可克，卻請他不要親征，煬帝當下變色；右尚方署監事耿詢上書切諫，被喝令斬首，靠少府監何稠苦救才得免。他的指揮作風也寫在詔令與戒勉之中：要求諸將分為三道，毋得輕軍獨進，軍事進止都要奏聞待報，圍城之中又反覆交代高麗若降即宜撫納。遼東城久攻不下，高句麗屢次假意請降，諸將不敢赴機，先請旨再進攻，一來一回守禦也就整備好了，六月己未煬帝親至城南觀形勢，當面斥責諸將自恃官高位重、意在暗懦待我，把行營駐在城西數里的六合城。真正決定戰局的是一批各懷脾氣的將領。宇文述領扶餘道主力，後來在軍中壓過眾議追擊乙支文德；于仲文領樂浪道，奉密旨本要擒下文德，卻被尚書右丞、慰撫使劉士龍固止，放文德渡鴨綠水而去；文德既走，仲文力主以精銳追之，責宇文述仗十萬之眾不能破小賊，何顏以見帝，述才被迫同行。追擊途中宇文述一日七戰皆捷，既恃驟勝又為眾議所迫，東渡薩水，在距平壤城三十里的山上設營，此時士卒已疲弊難戰，文德又遣使詐降，稱高元願到行在所朝見，述遂藉此退兵。七月戰敗回來，煬帝大怒把諸將鎖系，但因宇文述素有寵於帝、其子宇文士及尚帝女南陽公主，終不忍誅，只把宇文述、于仲文等除名為民；劉士龍被斬以謝天下，薛世雄因在白石山破高句麗追兵獨得免官，衛文昇因一軍獨全拜紫光祿大夫，眾將皆委罪於于仲文，煬帝獨系仲文，仲文憂恚成病，卒於家。左屯衛大將軍麥鐵杖在遼水搶渡時躍登東岸戰死，死前對三子說吾荷國恩、今為死日；左屯衛將軍辛世雄在薩水軍半渡之際戰死；江淮水軍主將來護兒在浿水破敵後不聽副總管周法尚俟諸軍至俱進之勸，率精甲四萬直抵城下，縱兵入城俘掠而失去部伍，中了羅郭內空寺的伏兵，僅以數千人退回。殿後的天水王仁恭在鴨綠水擊退追兵，才讓潰軍得以收攏；全軍唯一完整帶回來的，是增地道一路的衛文昇。左候衛大將軍段文振出南蘇道，路上上表請嚴勒諸軍、星馳速發、出其不意，卻在三月辛卯病歿道中，未及接戰。
peopleEn: This campaign was the making of Emperor Yang's will and the mistakes of a number of commanders alike. Yang issued the order on the renwu day of the first month, the first army marched on the guiwei day, and the imperial camp followed east, first sacrificing to Heaven at the Sanggan river, impersonating the Supreme Deity south of the Linshuo palace and sacrificing to the god of horses north of Jicheng, and only then breaking camp. Before departure he put to Geng Zhi, the magistrate of Heshui, the question whether the Goguryeo host could stand against a single commandery of his and whether the war could be won; Geng answered that it could be won, but asked the emperor not to come in person, and Yang's face darkened at this. Geng Xun, a supervisor in the Bureau of Imperial Workshops, memorialised in urgent remonstrance and was ordered to be beheaded, escaping only because the Master of Works He Chou pleaded for him. The emperor's way of command was written into his orders and his exhortations: the generals were to advance in three mutually supporting columns, were not to move in light force alone, and every move and halt of the army was to be reported and awaited; in the siege, he repeated that if Goguryeo surrendered it was to be received and pacified and the soldiers not allowed to plunder. Liaodong would not fall, and Goguryeo several times pretended to surrender, but the generals, afraid to act without leave, first sent riders to the emperor; by the time the answer came back the defences were repaired, and so the siege dragged on. In the sixth month, on the jiwei day, Yang came himself to the south of the city, looked over its position, and upbraided the generals for relying on their rank and family to treat him with slackness, and set up camp at the Liuhé city a few li west of the walls. The men who actually decided the battle were a set of commanders each with his own temper. Yuwen Shu led the main body on the Fuyu road and later overrode the general opinion in favour of pursuing Yizhi Wende; Yu Zhongwen, commanding on the Lelang road, had a secret order to seize Wende, but was prevented by the right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, Liu Shilong, who was serving as commissioner for pacification, and Wende was allowed to cross the Yalu. Once Wende had gone, Zhongwen argued for following him with picked troops and reproached Shu for being unable to break a small enemy with a hundred thousand men and for lacking the face to meet the emperor, and only then did Shu agree. In the pursuit, Yuwen Shu won seven engagements in a single day; emboldened by sudden success and pressed by the others, he crossed the Salu river eastward and encamped among the hills thirty li from the city of Pyongyang, where his soldiers were already exhausted and unable to fight, and Wende sent a second emissary to feign surrender, saying that Gao Yuan would come to the imperial camp; Shu took the pretext and withdrew. After the defeat in the seventh month the emperor was furious and had the generals put in chains, but because Yuwen Shu had long been favoured and his son Yuwen Shiji had married the emperor's daughter the Princess Nanyang, Yang could not bring himself to kill him, and merely stripped Yuwen Shu, Yu Zhongwen and the rest of their ranks; Liu Shilong was beheaded to satisfy the realm, Xue Shixiong alone was let off with a demotion because he had broken the Goguryeo pursuit at Baishi hill, Wei Wensheng was made Grand Master of the Purple Splendour because his one army came back intact, and all the generals shifted the blame onto Yu Zhongwen, whom the emperor alone kept in custody, until worry and rage brought on his illness and he died at home. Mai Tiezhang, commander of the Left Headquarters Guard, was killed leaping onto the east bank of the Liao river during the crossing, and before dying said to his three sons that he had received the empire's favour and that this was his day of death; Xin Shixiong, commander of the Left Headquarters Guard, was killed at the Salu while the army was half across; and Lai Hu'er, commanding the river fleet, broke the enemy at the Waidu river but would not listen to his deputy Zhou Fashang's advice to wait for the other armies, marched his forty thousand picked troops straight to the walls, let his men sack the city and lose all order, and fell into an ambush posted in the Kongsi temple inside the outer city, returning with only a few thousand men. Tiangui's Prince Ren Gong acted as the rearguard at the Yalu and beat back the pursuit, which allowed the broken army to be rallied; the only force that returned with its organisation intact was Wei Wensheng's column from the Zengdi road. Duan Wenzhen, commander of the Left Guard of the March, took the Nansu road and on the way memorialised that the armies be tightened and sent at full speed to take the enemy by surprise, yet he died of illness on the march on the xinmao day of the third month and never reached the fighting.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛是公元前九世紀兩河流域的兵器：短柄、長刃、配著鐵鏃，亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一處使用，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。它距大業八年的鴨綠水有一千五百餘年，不可能出現在這條戰線上；它在本役的位置，是作為長柄刃兵矛與槊之形制源流被提及：把鐵鏃套在木柄上的做法，自兩河流域傳到中原之後，就成了步兵與騎兵標準配備的槊頭。隋軍此役真正攜帶的裝備，見於出師的條目：鎧冑、纓拂、旗幡、戎具、火幕，以及槍、槊；糧秣是百日糧，人別三石以上，士卒重到不能勝致，軍中下令遺棄米粟者斬，於是把米穀埋進帳下的坑裡。排甲是這支大軍能連續行軍的關鍵：縱排的甲片繫在木條上，比整片甲冑適合長途與水陸轉進；騎兵四十隊、步卒八十隊各按團色分旗，行軍縱隊之中，輜重散兵另編四團由步卒挾帶，帳幕之間才搭得起火幕。攻城器械方面，遼水阻渡時由工部尚書宇文愷造浮橋三道，橋成而短於東岸丈餘，第一次接岸死傷慘重，後由何稠接手兩日而成，諸軍才得次第渡過；圍遼東城用的是常規攻器械具，具體名目在《資治通鑑》本役段落中沒有記載，直到大業九年再征同一座城時才記下飛樓、橦、雲梯、地道四面俱進、沖梯竿長十五丈，可作對照。江淮水軍則是另一套裝備系統：來護兒所帥的舳艫數百里，由東萊浮海入浿水，船上載的是水軍裝備與糧秣，卻在浿水一役中因縱兵掠城而失去部伍。高句麗那一邊靠的是自己的傳統：長弓大矢用於城頭與野戰射擊，步騎著皮甲札甲，城池依山傍水而守，平壤的城牆與周邊山川是他們的依托，伏兵與詐降是家常手段，糧秣靠城外的農業供應，而隋軍的糧秣自數千里外運來，兩者在補給上的差距，正是這場戰役的底色。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is a weapon of the Mesopotamian world of the ninth century BC: a short haft, a long blade, an iron socketed head, carried by the Assyrians together with the bow and iron tools, while the cities of the two rivers fell one after another. It stands more than fifteen hundred years before the Yalu in the eighth year of Daye and could not possibly have been on this front; its place in this campaign is as the source of the form of the long-hafted blade weapons, the mao and the spear: the practice of socketing an iron head onto a wooden shaft, carried from the two rivers into the Central Plain, became the standard head of the mao carried by foot and mounted troops alike. The equipment the Sui army actually carried in this campaign is listed in the orders for the march: armour, plumes, banners, accoutrements and fire-screens, together with spears and mao; for provisions, a hundred days of grain, more than three sheng per man, so heavy that no one could bear it, and the order in the camp was that anyone who threw away rice or millet would be beheaded, so the grain was buried in pits under the tents. The laminated armour was the key to the army's ability to keep marching: plates set on wooden strips in rows, far better suited to long marches and to movement by water and land than a solid coat; the forty cavalry units and eighty infantry units were each distinguished by the colour of their regimental banners, and inside the marching column the baggage troops and stragglers were formed into four more regiments carried along by the infantry, so that fire-screens could be pitched between the tents. On the assault side, when the Liao river blocked the crossing, the Minister of Works Yuwen Kai built three floating bridges; when they were finished they fell a zhang and more short of the eastern bank, and the first attempt to run them cost many men, until He Chou took over and finished in two days, after which the armies crossed in succession. The siege of Liaodong used ordinary assault equipment, but the specific names are not given in the Zizhi Tongjian for this campaign; they appear only when the same city was attacked again in the ninth year of Daye, when flying towers, ramming beams, cloud ladders and tunnels were pushed in on all four sides and the assault ladder was fifteen zhang long, which serves as a comparison. The river fleet under Lai Hu'er was a separate system of equipment: several hundred li of barges and light craft, sailing east from Donglai into the Waidu river, carrying naval gear and provisions, and yet at the Waidu it lost all order because the men were let off to sack the town. Goguryeo relied on its own tradition: long bows with heavy arrows used for shooting from the walls and in the open field; hide and lamellar armour for foot and horse; cities held where the mountains and waters allowed; the walls of Pyongyang and the hills around them as the framework of the defence; ambush and feigned surrender as ordinary methods; and grain from the farmland outside the walls, while the Sui army's grain came from hundreds of li away. The gap in supply between the two sides was the underlying condition of the whole campaign.
tactics: 隋軍的戰術框架是分道齊進、限期會合：日遣一軍，相去四十里，連營漸進，四十日發盡，旌旗亙九百六十里，御營再亙八十里，計畫是二十四路在平壤城下會師後一齊攻城。制度上的弱點從一開始就寫在詔令裡，不得輕軍獨進、軍止必奏，這在面對高句麗時成了最貴的束縛：遼東城將領屢屢請降，諸將先馳奏再赴機，等回報到時守禦已經整備完畢，攻城就這樣拖成了圍城。渡遼水的戰術最見技術含量：第一次用浮橋，橋短不及岸，隋兵爭赴水中接戰，被高處的高句麗兵居高打擊，麥鐵杖與錢士雄、孟叉等皆戰死；後由何稠主持重造，兩日而成，大軍才在東岸展開，把高句麗兵打死者以萬計，再乘勝圍遼東城。真正的崩潰發生在鴨綠水以西到薩水這一段：宇文述在乙支文德每戰輒走的節奏下追擊，一日七戰皆捷，既恃驟勝又為眾議所迫，東渡薩水、因山為營，距平壤城只剩三十里；此時文德二次遣使詐降，稱高元願到行在所朝見，述以士卒疲弊、平壤難拔為由退兵，退時為方陣而行，四面遭高句麗鈔擊，軍至薩水半渡之際後軍被擊，辛世雄戰死，諸軍遂不可禁止地潰散，一日一夜奔回鴨綠水，行四百五十里，王仁恭為殿才把追兵擊退。高句麗的戰術是一整套以空間換時間的消耗法：拒水斷渡、依城死守，不與隋軍決戰於城下，而以詐降拖住對手、以小股接戰疲其銳氣，待其糧盡人疲、進退失據，再在退路上集中兵力各擊一面；浿水一役，來護兒破敵之後追入城中，羅郭內空寺的伏兵隨即發作，正是這種預設退路再收網的打法。兩相比較，隋軍把優勢用在正面鋪開與正面攻擊，高句麗把優勢用在遲滯、伏擊與攻其必救，本役的勝負正是由這一點決定的。
tacticsEn: The Sui tactical framework was to advance in parallel columns and to converge at an appointed time: one army was sent off each day, each forty li behind the one before it, the camp following the camp in a continuous chain, so that the last of them left after forty days; the banners of the column ran for nine hundred and sixty li and the imperial camp for another eighty li behind that, and the plan was that the twenty-four columns would meet beneath Pyongyang and assault the city together. The weakness of the system was written into the orders from the start. No light force might move in alone, and every move of the army had to be reported and awaited; against Goguryeo this became the most expensive of restraints. The defenders of Liaodong repeatedly offered surrender, and the generals always sent riders to the emperor before acting, so that by the time the answer arrived the defences were ready, and the assault turned into a siege. The crossing of the Liao river was the moment of greatest technical ingenuity: the first attempt used the floating bridges, which fell short of the far bank, so that the Sui soldiers rushed into the water to fight and were struck from the heights by the Goguryeo troops; Mai Tiezhang, Qian Shixiong and Meng Cha died there. He Chou took over the work and finished in two days, the army then deployed on the eastern bank, killed Goguryeo troops by the tens of thousands, and closed on Liaodong in pursuit. The real collapse happened between the Yalu and the Salu. Under the rhythm of Yizhi Wende, who gave ground at every engagement, Yuwen Shu pressed the pursuit and won seven engagements in a single day; emboldened by sudden success and pressed by the other officers, he crossed the Salu and encamped among the hills, only thirty li from Pyongyang, where his men were worn out; Wende then sent a second emissary to feign surrender, saying that Gao Yuan would come to court, and Shu, seeing his troops spent and the city hard to take, turned back. His withdrawal was made in a square formation, and Goguryeo struck at it from all four sides; at the Salu, with half the army still across, the rearguard was hit, Xin Shixiong was killed, the armies dissolved beyond all control, and the soldiers ran back to the Yalu, four hundred and fifty li in a single day and night, only to have the pursuit driven off by Prince Ren Gong acting as rearguard. Goguryeo's method was a whole technique of trading space for time: refusing the crossing, holding the cities, refusing to give battle beneath the walls, delaying the enemy with feigned surrender, wearing down the edge of their spirit with small engagements, waiting until their food was gone and their men weary and their movements disordered, and then concentrating on one flank of the line of retreat; at the Waidu, after Lai Hu'er had broken the enemy and chased them into the town, the ambush hidden in the Kongsi temple inside the outer city sprang out, which was exactly that method of preparing the ground and then closing the net. The contrast is plain: the Sui army spent its advantage on frontal deployment and frontal attack, while Goguryeo spent its advantage on delay, ambush and strikes on the over-extended. That single point decided the campaign.
data: 可查的數字大致如下。出師之眾，《資治通鑑》記為一百一十三萬三千八百人，號二百萬，其饋運者倍之，這是隋代記載中規模最大的一次用兵；分左右各十二軍，共二十四道，御營合十一衛、三台、五省、九寺分隸六軍。每軍編制為大將、亞將各一人，騎兵四十隊、每隊百人、十隊為團，步卒八十隊分為四團，輜重散兵另為四團，合計每軍步騎萬人上下。行軍序列是日遣一軍、相去四十里、連營漸進，四十日而發盡，旌旗連亙九百六十里，御營再亙八十里，煬帝稱近古出師之盛、未之有也。糧秣方面，宇文述等自瀘河、懷遠二鎮出發時，人馬皆給百日糧，另給排甲、槍槊、衣資、戎具、火幕，士卒人別三石以上，重莫能勝致，結果才行及中路，糧已將盡。損耗方面最硬的一組數字是：初九軍渡遼凡三十萬五千人，及還至遼東城只剩二千七百人；左屯衛大將軍麥鐵杖與虎賁郎將錢士雄、孟叉在遼水搶渡時戰死，左屯衛將軍辛世雄在薩水戰死；江淮水軍主將來護兒所部精甲四萬，士卒還者不過數千人；高句麗在遼水東岸一戰死者萬計。距離與時間上，隋軍進至遼水，麥鐵杖等戰死於此；段文振三月辛卯卒於南蘇道；六月己未煬帝幸遼東城南；七月壬寅薩水之潰；大軍一日一夜奔至鴨綠水，行四百五十里；浿水距平壤六十里，薩水距平壤城三十里；遼水浮橋短於東岸丈餘；八月敕運黎陽、洛陽、太原等倉谷向望海頓，樊子蓋留守涿郡；九月庚寅車駕至東都；十一月以宗女為華容公主嫁高昌。收穫方面，是行只拔高麗武歷邏一城，置遼東郡及通定鎮而已。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The strength of the expedition is recorded in the Zizhi Tongjian as one million one hundred and thirty-three thousand eight hundred men, nominally two hundred thousand, with the supply column twice that number, which makes it the largest deployment in Sui records; there were twelve armies on the left and twelve on the right, twenty-four columns in all, and the imperial camp combined the eleven guards, the three platforms, the five ministries and the nine temples across the inner, outer, front, rear, left and right armies. Each army had one commander and one deputy, forty cavalry units of a hundred men each with ten units to a regiment, eighty infantry units divided into four regiments, and four regiments of baggage troops and stragglers, giving some ten thousand foot and horse per army. The order of march was one army a day, each forty li behind the last, the camps continuous, the last army leaving after forty days; the banners ran for nine hundred and sixty li and the imperial camp for another eighty li beyond that, and the emperor called it the greatest expedition since ancient times. On provisions, the troops leaving from the two garrisons of the Lu and Huai rivers were each given a hundred days of grain, together with laminated armour, spears and mao, clothing, accoutrements and fire-screens, more than three sheng per man, so heavy that no one could bear it, and the result was that the grain was already nearly spent by the middle of the road. The hardest figures are those of the losses: of the nine armies that crossed the Liao river, numbering three hundred and five thousand men, only two thousand seven hundred returned as far as Liaodong; Mai Tiezhang, with the tiger guards Qian Shixiong and Meng Cha, were killed at the crossing of the Liao, and Xin Shixiong was killed at the Salu; of the forty thousand picked troops with which Lai Hu'er advanced, the men who came back numbered only a few thousand; and in the battle on the east bank of the Liao the Goguryeo dead were counted by the ten thousands. On distance and time: the Sui army reached the Liao river, where Mai Tiezhang was killed; Duan Wenzhen died on the Nansu road on the xinmao day of the third month; on the jiwei day of the sixth month the emperor came to the south of Liaodong; on the renyin day of the seventh month came the rout at the Salu; the army ran to the Yalu, four hundred and fifty li, in a day and a night; the Waidu river was sixty li from Pyongyang and the Salu thirty li from the city; the floating bridges on the Liao fell more than a zhang short of the eastern bank; in the eighth month an order was issued to move grain from the granaries of Liyang, Luoyang and Taiyuan to Wanghaidun, with Fan Zikai left in charge of Zhuo; on the gengyin day of the ninth month the imperial carriage reached the eastern capital; and in the eleventh month a daughter of the imperial clan was sent as the Princess Huarong to marry the king of Gaochang. As for what was gained, the campaign took only the one city of Wuliluo and established the commandery of Liaodong and the garrison town of Tongding.
cause: 開打的原因有遠有近。遠因是隋朝自開皇末年以來就沒有解決東北問題：開皇十八年（598）第一次大舉征高句麗便是大敗而歸，煬帝即位後把這筆帳算在高句麗頭上，視之為新王朝的奇恥。近因是外交上的僵局，高句麗不奉隋朝的詔令，也不接受隋廷對邊市與使節往來的安排，兩國往來中斷，隋朝無法容忍一個邊國用這樣的方式把自己關在門外。更深的一層是地緣：高句麗扼守遼東山地與鴨綠水天險，控住從幽州通往東北的孔道，隋朝通往渤海、靺鞨、室韋的使節與物資都要經過其境；段文振在出師前上表也提到，若不能速戰，一旦秋雨綿綿、兵糧既竭、強敵在前而靺鞨出後，就再沒有好辦法。煬帝本人的心理也是關鍵：他不接受兵多而不精之策，覺得拔海移山都做得到，一個小國自然不在話下；庚質請他不要親征、耿詢上書切諫，都被喝退。於是這一役不是一次有明確終點的軍事行動，而是天子把國運壓上去的一次賭注。百濟的加入使局面更複雜：百濟王璋請討高句麗、派國智牟來請師期，隋廷大喜，厚加賞賜並派起部郎席律告知會期，卻不知璋同時與高句麗潛通，隋軍渡遼之後百濟在國境上嚴兵、聲稱助隋，實際持兩端，等於隋軍的側翼從頭到尾都沒有真正打開。
causeEn: The reasons were both near and far. The distant reason is that the Sui had never settled the northeastern question since the end of the Kaihuang era: the first great campaign against Goguryeo in the eighteenth year of Kaihuang (598) had ended in a rout, and once he came to the throne Yang charged that debt to Goguryeo and treated it as the new dynasty's standing disgrace. The nearer reason was a diplomatic deadlock. Goguryeo did not obey the Sui summons, nor accept the Sui court's arrangement of the frontier markets and the passage of envoys; intercourse between the two states was broken off, and the Sui court could not tolerate a border kingdom shutting the door on it in this manner. Deeper still was the geography: Goguryeo held the mountains of Liaodong and the natural barrier of the Yalu, controlling the corridor from You prefecture into the northeast, and the Sui envoys and goods bound for the Bohai, the Jiewei and the Shiren had all to pass through its territory. Duan Wenzhen, in his memorial before the army set out, warned that if the war could not be hurried, then with autumn rain, exhausted supplies, the enemy in front and the Jiewei behind, no good plan would remain. The emperor's own state of mind was also decisive: he rejected the counsel that massed numbers without discipline would fail, judged that if mountains could be moved then a small kingdom was plainly beneath contempt, and sent back both Geng Zhi's request that he should not come in person and Geng Xun's written remonstrance. The campaign was therefore not a military operation with a defined end, but a wager in which the emperor staked the fortune of the dynasty. Baekje's involvement complicated the picture further: King Zhang asked to join the war against Goguryeo and sent Guozhi Mou to ask for the date, the Sui court was delighted, rewarded him lavishly and sent the director Xi Lü to announce the appointed time, unaware that Zhang was in secret communication with Goguryeo; after the Sui army crossed the Liao, Baekje merely massed troops on its frontier and professed to assist, in fact holding to both sides, so that the Sui flank was never truly opened at any point in the campaign.
impact: 這一仗的後果遠大於一場邊境挫折的分量。就隋朝而言，國力第一次被這種規模的遠征抽到底：三十萬五千人渡遼，回來二千七百人，資儲器械巨萬計、失亡蕩盡，平壤與遼東城都沒有拿下，實際收穫只有武歷邏一城與遼東郡、通定鎮兩個建置。河北與山東為了轉輸糧秣而被攤派更重，同一年大旱、疫癘流行，山東尤其嚴重，軍隊未發而後方先病。政治上，煬帝的威信第一次被打穿，諸將被鎖系，除名為民者比比皆是，陣亡者與陣亡將士的家人成為朝議的焦點；但他沒有收手，大業九年（613）再發大軍討高句麗，同樣在平壤一線潰敗，迫使第三次出兵，直到大業十年才以高句麗請和罷兵。真正致命的後果出現在大業九年：楊玄感以督運之名在黎陽起兵，打出誅除無道的旗號，河北山東盜賊蜂起，一半因為三年之內三次大規模徵調已把地方抽空；第二年再伐高句麗時，楊玄感故意逗留漕運，令渡遼諸軍乏食，隋朝的後方與糧道同時出問題。此後隋朝只能用臨時徵募的驍果與各地盜賊、叛軍周旋，兵制與財政都不可逆地崩壞，618年隋朝覆亡，東北戰線上的失敗只是這條下坡路的第一級台階。就高句麗而言，這是一場慘勝：平壤、鴨綠水與遼東都守住了，代價是遼水東岸一役死者萬計，七年之後又要再遭隋軍傾國來攻，但國力得以保存，還藉隋朝的失敗坐穩了東北的宗主地位，往後百年仍能與唐朝相抗，最終在唐高宗總章元年（668）為唐所滅。往遠處看，這一役也把東北亞的政治格局推到另一個階段：隋朝的軍隊退過鴨綠水之後，渤海、靺鞨、高句麗、扶餘等政權在東北亞各占其地，而唐王朝日後要以另一種方式重新處理同一片山地與天險。
impactEn: The consequences of this defeat weighed far more than a border reverse. For the Sui, the strength of the state was drained to the bottom for the first time by an expedition of this scale: three hundred and five thousand men crossed the Liao river and two thousand seven hundred came back, the stores and equipment worth tens of thousands were lost entirely, neither Pyongyang nor Liaodong was taken, and the whole gain was the one city of Wuliluo together with the commandery of Liaodong and the garrison town of Tongding. Hebei and Shandong, whose task it was to haul the grain, were ground down by heavier levies, and in that same year there was a great drought and an outbreak of sickness, worst of all in Shandong, so that the rear areas fell ill before the army had even set out. Politically the emperor's prestige was broken for the first time: the generals were put in chains, the number of men stripped of rank was large, and the killed and the families of the killed became the focus of debate at court. He did not stop, however. In the ninth year of Daye (613) he raised another great army against Goguryeo and was routed again on the Pyongyang line, which forced a third expedition, and only in the tenth year of Daye was the war ended when Goguryeo sued for peace. The fatal consequences came in that ninth year: Yang Xuanggan rose in Liyang under cover of superintending the transport, calling for the destruction of the tyrant; bandits rose in numbers all over Hebei and Shandong, in part because three great levies within three years had drained the districts; and when the campaign against Goguryeo was mounted again, Yang Xuanggan deliberately held back the grain convoy so that the armies beyond the Liao would go hungry, so that the rear of the Sui and its supply line failed at the same time. Thereafter the Sui could only fight with ad hoc levies, with the picked guards and with the bandits and rebels of the provinces, and both the military system and the finances collapsed irreversibly; the dynasty fell in 618, and the failure on the northeastern front was only the first step down that slope. For Goguryeo it was a costly victory: Pyongyang, the Yalu and Liaodong were all held, at the price of Goguryeo dead counted by the ten thousands on the east bank of the Liao and of facing another all-out Sui invasion seven years later, but the state's strength was preserved and it took over the position of overlord in the northeast on the strength of the Sui failure, holding out against the Tang for another century until it was destroyed in the first year of Zongzhang (668). In the longer view, the campaign pushed the political pattern of Northeast Asia into another phase: once the Sui armies withdrew beyond the Yalu, the Bohai, the Jiewei, Goguryeo and Buyeo each took their own ground in Northeast Asia, and the Tang court would later have to handle the same mountains and the same natural barriers by a different route.
result: 大業八年（612）這一季的結局是隋軍的大敗。平壤沒有攻下，遼東城沒有攻下，遼水東岸雖然打了一場勝仗，卻換來薩水的一場潰滅：七月壬寅，宇文述所部行至薩水半渡，後軍被高句麗兵擊中，左屯衛將軍辛世雄戰死，諸軍一齊崩潰，不可禁止，士卒一日一夜奔回鴨綠水，行四百五十里之後才停下來。撤退途中天水王仁恭為殿，擊退高句麗追兵；江淮水軍的來護兒聽聞敗訊引還，屯海浦不敢復留；全軍之中只有增地道的衛文昇一軍完整帶回。前面的損耗數字說明了一切：九軍渡遼三十萬五千人，還到遼東城時剩二千七百人。這一場敗仗對隋廷的直接處置是：煬帝聞訊大怒，鎖系宇文述等諸將，九月庚寅回到東都；因宇文述素有寵於帝、其子士及尚南陽公主，最終不忍誅，只把宇文述、于仲文等除名為民，斬劉士龍以謝天下，薛世雄因破高麗追兵獨得免官，衛文昇因一軍獨全升為紫光祿大夫；諸將皆委罪於于仲文，煬帝獨系仲文，仲文憂恚成病，卒於家。戰後的實際收穫只有兩個地名：拔高麗武歷邏，置遼東郡及通定鎮。對高句麗來說，這是守住國門的一役；對隋朝來說，這是三次征高句麗中最慘的一次，也是隋朝由盛轉衰的分水嶺之一，從此以後東北方向再也沒有打過這樣的仗，隋廷把力氣轉回關內，而關內的局勢已在楊玄感的起兵與遍地的盜賊中成形，四年後隋朝亡於江都之變。
resultEn: The outcome of the campaign of 612 was a Sui defeat. Pyongyang was not taken and Liaodong was not taken; the victory won on the east bank of the Liao river was paid for by the destruction at the Salu. On the renyin day of the seventh month, half of Yuwen Shu's army was across the Salu when the rearguard was struck by Goguryeo troops, Xin Shixiong was killed, the armies broke up beyond all control, and the soldiers ran back to the Yalu, four hundred and fifty li, before they could be stopped. On the retreat, Prince Ren Gong of Tiangui acted as rearguard and beat off the pursuit; Lai Hu'er of the river fleet withdrew on hearing of the defeat and halted at Haipu, no longer daring to stay to support the others; of the whole army only Wei Wensheng's column from the Zengdi road came back with its organisation intact. The loss figures set out above make the outcome plain: of the three hundred and five thousand men with which nine armies crossed the Liao, two thousand seven hundred reached Liaodong again. The court's direct response to the defeat was as follows. The emperor was furious, had Yuwen Shu and the other generals put in chains, and reached the eastern capital on the gengyin day of the ninth month. Because Yuwen Shu had long been favoured and his son Shiji had married the Princess Nanyang, Yang could not bring himself to execute him; the men were stripped of rank and sent into the ranks of the commoners, Liu Shilong was beheaded to satisfy the realm, Xue Shixiong alone was let off with a demotion for breaking the Goguryeo pursuit, and Wei Wensheng was raised to Grand Master of the Purple Splendour for bringing his one army back whole. All the generals shifted the blame on Yu Zhongwen, whom the emperor alone kept in custody until anxiety and rage brought on his illness and he died at home. The whole material gain of the campaign amounted to two place names: the taking of Wuliluo and the establishment of the commandery of Liaodong and the garrison town of Tongding. For Goguryeo this was a battle to hold the gate of the country; for the Sui it was the most ruinous of the three campaigns against Goguryeo and one of the watersheds between the dynasty's strength and its decline. No comparable expedition was ever mounted in that quarter again, the Sui court turned its strength back towards the interior, and the situation inside the passes had already been shaped by Yang Xuanggan's revolt and the bandits scattered over the provinces; four years later the Sui fell in the coup at Jiangdu.
